sections.name: File setup, STEPS
sections.title: Imports, owner check and step names
sections.what: Brings in the profile helpers and the role types, defines a hardcoded personal email address, and lists the six onboarding step names.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The personal email is visible in shipped browser code, so it should not decide access on its own.

sections.name: RoleConfig
sections.title: Shape of role hint data
sections.what: Describes what each role's hints contain: skill groups, and sample text for strengths, exit story, target roles and headline.
sections.why: Gives the form example text for each job family.
sections.watch_out: Each role needs every one of these fields, or the page breaks.

sections.name: ROLE_CONFIGS (part 1)
sections.title: Example hints for the first five roles
sections.what: Gives sample skills, strengths, career goals and headlines for strategy consulting, AI tech, product, engineering and design.
sections.why: Sample text guides users who are unsure what to write.
sections.watch_out: These are sample words shown in fields, not saved values, so the user must replace them.

sections.name: ROLE_CONFIGS (part 2)
sections.title: Example hints for the last five roles
sections.what: Gives the same kind of sample hints for marketing, sales, finance, operations and data.
sections.why: Keeps the form relevant to each job family.
sections.watch_out: The type requires every role key, so adding a role to the profile library needs a matching entry here.

sections.name: ROLE_CONFIGS (part 3)
sections.title: Role-specific wording for each career type
sections.what: Holds the wording for each career type (research, creative, other): the skill category names, example text, and headline and summary prompts. The setup screens read these values, so editing a line here changes what the user sees.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the wording for each career type in one place so the screens do not need separate code for each type.
sections.watch_out: Each career type needs all four skill categories and every placeholder, or the form will show blank labels or prompts.

sections.name: blankProfile
sections.title: Empty starting profile
sections.what: Creates a blank profile with every field empty, and sets the created and updated times to now. The setup screens start from this blank profile before the user types anything.
sections.why: Gives the form a complete shape so every field has a value to read and update.
sections.watch_out: A new profile field must be added here too, or the form may read it as missing.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 1)
sections.title: Setup page state and login pre-fill
sections.what: Holds the current step, the profile being built, the uploaded resume text, and upload status. On load it asks the server who is logged in and fills in the email field from that answer.
sections.why: Pre-filling the email from the login saves the user from typing it again.
sections.watch_out: If the login check fails, the error is silently ignored and the email field stays empty.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 2)
sections.title: Resume upload and finish actions
sections.what: Reads uploaded text and markdown files directly, sends images to the extract-resume service for text, and rejects other types such as PDFs with a message. The finish action saves the profile, stores the first 8000 characters of resume text, and opens the home page.
sections.why: Likely reason: PDFs are not read in this code, so the message asks users to screenshot them instead.
sections.watch_out: Each upload is added to the existing resume text, so uploading the same file twice adds a duplicate copy.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 3)
sections.title: Shared input styles and page frame
sections.what: Sets the common look for inputs and labels, then draws the page header, a welcome banner, the step progress bar, and the card that holds each step.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the repeated styles in one place so every field looks the same.
sections.watch_out: The welcome banner is tied to one hardcoded account email, so this personal shortcut would show to every user.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 4)
sections.title: Career type selection step
sections.what: Shows the career types as selectable cards. Picking one sets the user's role, which decides the wording on later steps.
sections.why: Lets the rest of the form match its examples to the user's field.
sections.watch_out: The Next button stays disabled until a career type is chosen, so this step cannot be skipped.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 5)
sections.title: Identity and target role steps
sections.what: Step 1 collects name, email, phone, location, and profile links. Step 2 collects the locations the user is open to and a free text box for target roles.
sections.why: Splits the form into short screens so each one asks related questions.
sections.watch_out: The target role text is saved into voice notes, and the finish step replaces voice notes with resume text when a resume is present, so the target role text can be lost.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 6)
sections.title: Narrative step: headline, superpowers, exit story
sections.what: Collects a one-line headline, three to five superpowers, and an exit story. Superpowers and exit story are stored in the skills map under fixed keys.
sections.why: The page notes say the exit story is used in cover letters and outreach, so it is written as a forward-looking story.
sections.watch_out: These values sit in the skills map with the skill categories, so the profile editor lists them as if they were skill categories.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 7)
sections.title: Pay and remote work step
sections.what: Collects target pay, minimum pay, and a remote work preference chosen from a list. Each value is stored in the skills map under a fixed key.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Pay is free text, so the app cannot compare amounts or currencies from this screen.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 8)
sections.title: Resume upload and text box step
sections.what: Shows the upload button, the names of uploaded files, any upload error, and the resume text box with its character count.
sections.why: Lets the user upload a resume or paste it, and see what was captured.
sections.watch_out: Uploads and pasted text share one box, so an upload adds to anything already typed.

sections.name: OnboardPage (part 9)
sections.title: Skill entry boxes and step buttons
sections.what: Shows one text box per skill category for the chosen career type, with comma-separated values. It also draws the BACK, NEXT, and FINISH buttons, and the note that the profile can be edited later.
sections.why: Lets each career type use its own skill categories while the buttons move the user through the steps.
sections.watch_out: Category names come from the career type settings, so renaming one there leaves old saved values under the old name, where they no longer appear.

summary: The onboarding form that builds the user's professional profile in six steps, with example hints for each role family. Only four of the fifteen sections were visible, so most of the file is unknown.
purpose: Collects the user's profile details in steps.
why: Likely reason: a profile is needed for scoring jobs, and guided steps make it easier to fill in.
how: Visible parts only: the list of six step names, a shape that describes hint data, and a table of example hints for each of ten role families. The step handling, saving and the rest of the form are not visible.
inputs: Not fully visible. Role choice and typed profile fields are likely.
outputs: Not fully visible. The hints appear as sample text inside fields, and saving is done through the profile helper.
risks: A hardcoded personal email address is in the file. Missing role entries break the type check. The unseen sections may hold more risks.
debug: If a role shows no hints, check its entry in the hint table. If the type check fails after adding a role, add a matching hint entry. For save problems, read the unseen sections of this file and the profile library.
